configurations.// native-tunnel: Expo Go over an ngrok tunnel — works when the phone is NOT on the same WiFi as this machine (mobile data, guest network, VPN). Slower to boot and to reload than --lan; prefer 'native' when both devices share a network. Requires the @expo/ngrok devDependency.
configurations.name: native-tunnel

configurations.// web-mock: UI verification only. Separate port so it never disturbs the native LAN server the phone is attached to, and EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH=true so the tabs are reachable without a real sign-in (shell env beats .env; inert outside __DEV__).
configurations.name: web-mock

configurations.// web-signedout: Web build WITHOUT EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH, so the auth gate treats the session as signed out. Needed to reach /welcome and /auth, which mock-auth skips past. Own port so it never collides with web-mock (8091) or the native LAN server (8090).
configurations.name: web-signedout

configurations.// web-dist: Serves the PRODUCTION export in dist/ exactly as Vercel will, with -s (SPA fallback) mirroring the vercel.json rewrite. Use this to catch runtime crashes that only appear in a minified production bundle.
configurations.name: web-dist
